name: qof-register-builder
description: Builds NHS QOF-style disease registers from SNOMED-coded synthetic records and deterministically flags miscoded free text (with the exact suggested code) and status conflicts — the LLM only drafts the completeness report, verified against the computed results. Demo. FastAPI + Next.js.

paragraphs: A QOF-style disease-register builder + miscoding flagger for a synthetic GP practice. A deterministic engine builds the disease registers from real SNOMED CT codes (per a committed register-definition table) and decides every data-quality flag — free-text problems that exactly match a known SNOMED synonym but carry no code, and concepts recorded both active and resolved. The LLM only drafts the register-completeness report and per-patient correction explanations, behind a deterministic grounding gate: it can never mention a patient id, code, or register that isn't in the computed results.

Built around one idea: measure LLM systems, don't vibe them. In a clinical-coding product the facts — who is on a register, which code is missing — must be decided in code, not by a model. The model's job is the prose; the gate makes sure the prose can't invent facts.
